messages: Board lead: I can cut A_board from 1250 to 1205 mm², which gives 2699 mm³ (-101 mm³). Routability should stay just above 0.95. I won't go lower, because the floor is about 1197 mm² and I want a little margin. That covers only about 8% of the 1246 mm³ overage, so the rest has to come from the other domains. Battery at 3786 mm³ and antenna plus NFC at 2000 mm³ are the largest blocks. Since GNSS L5 is the top priority, antenna volume should be protected, and I suggest the other cuts come from battery, acoustics and structure. I'll OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Battery lead: I'm at 59.78 h on 3786 mm³, with 4.73 mm thickness and the z-stack OK. That is essentially at the 60 h target, and the siren's 3 h endurance draws on the same cell energy. Every mm³ I give up costs runtime, so I can't make the big cut alone. I support protecting antenna volume, since L5 is the top priority. The remaining overage is 1145 mm³, so structure, acoustics, thermal and haptics need to trim too. I'm probing 3600, 3500 and 3400 mm³ to find my runtime slope, and I'll offer a concrete cut next round. Caseback is 1120 of 1143 mm², so my footprint can't grow by more than 23 mm².

Antenna lead: I'm holding V_ant at 1500 mm³ for now. L5 efficiency is only 0.208, so I won't cut until I see my slope. Probing 1200 and 1800 mm³ will show the volume slope.

Thinner walls look like the best lever on both fronts. Each -0.1 mm of wall frees 150 mm³ for the interior, and it should reduce detuning of the antenna. I'm probing t_wall at 1.0 and 1.1 mm. Structure lead, please report the stiffness and drop-test margin at 1.1 and 1.0 mm.

NFC lead: your 500 mm³ shares the 2400 mm³ perimeter with me. We are at 1820 of 2400, so the perimeter is fine for now.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Thermal lead: I'm at 320 mm² (250 mm³), and skin temperature is exactly 43.0 °C, so I have no margin. Any cut to A_spr breaks the limit at the current 1.2 mm wall. The spreader is only 250 of the 12,345 mm³ claimed, so I can't close the overage. Thermal can't cover the 1,145 mm³ gap on its own.

Wall thickness affects my temperature, so I'm probing t_wall at 1.1 and 1.0 mm. If a thinner wall leaves margin, I can trade spreader area for volume. I'll also test 300 mm² at 1.1 mm. Structure lead, please report the stiffness and drop-test margin at 1.1 and 1.0 mm.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed. My own requirement is met.

Structure lead: my pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 requirement, so I fail at 1.2 mm wall, 1800 mm³ ribs and a 9 mm² port. I can't offer thinner walls yet, and 1.1 mm probably makes the margin worse. I'm probing three things:
- **Rib slope:** 2000 mm³ of ribs at 1.2 mm wall.
- **Port slope:** a 7 mm² port with my current claims.
- **Ribs for wall:** 2200 mm³ of ribs at 1.1 mm wall.

Ribs cost 1 mm³ per mm³, while wall costs 150 mm³ per 0.1 mm, so ribs may be the cheaper way to buy margin. If the port slope is steep, a smaller port is the cheapest fix for me. Acoustics, please say what a port of 7-8 mm² costs you in siren dB and voice intelligibility. I'll hold my claims until the probes come back, and I OBJECT because my own requirement fails.

Acoustics: my siren fails badly. It needs 9.08 W against a 1.0 W limit, so endurance is only 0.34 h. Voice SII is fine at 88.8. Resonance is 5581 Hz with Q 3.72, so I'm probably tuned far from the siren's sweet spot, and mesh loss is likely costing me too.

Structure, I can't commit to a 7 mm² port yet. A smaller port usually raises siren power unless I retune. My probes test this:
- Mesh at its 20 rayl floor.
- A larger port with a longer outlet.
- A smaller cavity with a 7 mm² port.

Volume is negotiable once I find the slope. I'll likely give up 200-400 mm³ if the siren can be fixed by tuning rather than size.

I OBJECT because my own requirement fails.

Haptics: my force is 1.069 N at 350 mm³, against a 0.9 N requirement. The 0.9 N floor is about 295 mm³, so I can give back volume now. I'm claiming 315 mm³, a 35 mm³ cut that should leave about 0.95 N. My probes at 295, 305 and 330 will confirm the slope.

I can't go below about 300 mm³ without losing margin. Haptics is only about 3% of the interior, so the overage has to come from the larger blocks.

Since L5 is the top priority, antenna volume should be the last to be cut. I support wall, rib, port and acoustic retuning as the main levers.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed. My own requirement is met.

NFC lead: my read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement, so I have real slack and will give it back. I'm cutting from 500 to 410 mm³ now (loop 260, ferrite 150), a saving of 90 mm³. That also frees perimeter keepout for the antenna. I can't be sure of the slope until the probes come back. I'm probing 180/110 (the floor), 220/130 and 250/150. If the floor still reads above 10 mm, I'll drop to it next round, which would save up to 210 mm³ in total. My own requirement is met, but I OBJECT while the interior is still over-committed.

Board: I'm cutting A_board from 1205 to 1200 mm², which gives 2688 mm³ (-11 mm³). Routability is about 0.952 there, interpolated from my probes: 0.950 at 1197 and 0.956 at 1205. That is the end of my slack, since 1197 is the hard floor.

The interior is still over by about 1009 mm³, and the board can't close it. L5 is the top priority and antenna efficiency is only 0.208, so I'd rather the antenna get volume than lose it. The big cuts need to come from acoustics (if tuning fixes the siren), structure (a smaller port or ribs instead of wall), battery, and NFC's floor. I'll hold at 1200 unless someone finds that my area is blocking something.

My requirement is met, but I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Battery lead: the runtime slope from my probes is about 0.0158 h per mm³, or roughly 1.6 h per 100 mm³. Area barely matters, since thickness stays within limits down to 760 mm². I'm at 59.78 h, so every cut takes me below 60 h. The same cell energy also drives siren endurance, and acoustics currently needs 9 W against a 1 W limit.

I'll hold 3786 mm³ this round, and I'm not the place for the 1000 mm³ cut. The larger sources are:
- NFC dropping to its floor (about 120 mm³ more).
- Acoustics giving up 200-400 mm³.
- Structure trading ribs and port against wall.
- Antenna volume once its slope is known.

I'm probing 3700 mm³ at A_batt 800 and 840, and 3786 mm³ at A_batt 700.

Antenna: my L5 slope is diminishing. Efficiency is 0.133 at 1200 mm³, 0.208 at 1500 and 0.249 at 1800. That is about 0.00025 per mm³ below 1500 and 0.00014 per mm³ above it. Going from 1.2 to 1.0 mm wall adds +0.019 at 1500 mm³. That is worth about 100-140 mm³ of antenna volume, and it frees 300 mm³ for everyone. L5 is the top priority, so I'm holding 1500 and won't be the main donor.

Perimeter is fine: 1910 of 2400 mm³ with NFC at 410. Structure, please say whether ribs can replace wall thickness. I'm probing 1400 mm³ and 1650 mm³, plus 1350 mm³ at a 1.0 mm wall, to see whether thinner wall lets me give volume back.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Thermal: I'm at my floor. Skin temperature is 43.00 °C at 320 mm² and a 1.2 mm wall. The spreader slope is about 0.012 °C per mm², so 300 mm² reads 43.23 °C and fails. A thinner wall barely helps me, giving only -0.02 °C at 1.1 mm and -0.03 °C at 1.0 mm. That means I can't donate volume. Thermal also has no objection to a thinner wall, because thermally it's nearly neutral. Structure, antenna and battery can negotiate the wall without worrying about me. The 250 mm³ spreader is only about 2% of the interior, so the 1,009 mm³ overage must come from other domains. If a thinner wall gives margin, I'll trim a few mm² at 1.0 mm. My probes test that.

Structure: the pressure data points to the port, not the wall.

- **Port:** about +0.062 margin per mm² removed.
- **Ribs:** only about 0.008 margin per 100 mm³. Cutting ribs from 1800 to 1400 frees 400 mm³ and costs roughly 0.03 margin.
- **Wall:** -0.1 mm costs about 0.19 margin, so I'm holding 1.2 mm.

My proposal is ribs 1400 and a port of 7.0-7.3 mm², which gives a margin of about 1.51-1.53.

NFC: I'm dropping to my floor, with loop 180 and ferrite 110. My probe at that point read 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, so the requirement is still met with about 27% margin. This saves another 120 mm³, 210 mm³ in total from my original 500, and NFC drops to 290 mm³.

The perimeter keepout also loosens: NFC's share falls from 410 to 290 mm³, which leaves the antenna more room if it needs it. I can't give anything more, because 110 is the ferrite floor and 180 is the loop floor.

The interior is still over by about 870 mm³ after this cut. The remaining cuts have to come from structure (ribs 1400, smaller port), acoustics and battery. I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Board: I'm trimming A_board from 1200 to 1198 mm², which gives about 2683 mm³ (-5 mm³). Routability there is 0.951, confirmed by probe. I'll probe 1197 and 1196 to verify the floor. I won't go below 1197 because 0.950 is the limit.

The board has nothing more to give. The interior is still about 870 mm³ over on the ledger, and the cuts that remain are:
- **Structure:** ribs to 1400 and a port of about 7 mm². That is 400 mm³ for roughly 0.03 margin.
- **Acoustics:** 200-400 mm³ from a siren redesign that fixes the 9 W draw against the 1 W limit.
- **Antenna and battery:** whatever their probes show.

L5 stays protected, so I'd rather the antenna keep its 1500 mm³. My requirement is met, but I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Battery: the runtime slope is confirmed at about 0.0158 h/mm³ (3700 → 58.42 h, 3786 → 59.78 h). Thickness is simply V/A (3786/800 = 4.73 mm), so area costs me nothing until thickness reaches 4.8 mm. A_batt can't go below about 790 mm², and 700 mm² failed the stack. I'm holding 3786 mm³ at 800 mm². That is already 0.2 h short of 60 h, so I can't donate volume.

The remaining 869 mm³ has to come from these sources:
- **Structure:** ribs to 1400 mm³ (-400) and a port of about 7 mm².
- **Acoustics:** the 9 W siren draw has to be redesigned, and I'd like to see that volume come out of acoustics.
- **Wall at 1.0 mm:** this frees about 300 mm³ for everyone, but structure and antenna need to settle it.

This round I'm probing 3800 mm³ at 820 mm², 3750 mm³ at 800 mm², and 3786 mm³ at 790 mm².

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Antenna: my L5 efficiency is 0.208 at 1500 mm³ and a 1.2 mm wall. That is the top-priority metric, so I'm holding V_ant at 1500 and not donating volume.

Structure is the better lever. Ribs at 1400 and a port near 7 mm² free about 400 mm³. A 1.0 mm wall frees about 300 mm³ more, for a structure cost of about 0.19 margin. That still leaves roughly 1.3 against about 1.5 now, assuming the port and ribs cuts land as structure estimates. I'd rather take that than cut antenna volume.

At a 1.0 mm wall my efficiency should rise to about 0.227, and 1350 mm³ already beats today's 1400 mm³ reading (0.185 vs 0.181). Structure, please confirm that 1.0 mm passes. The remaining overage then falls to roughly 170 mm³, which acoustics must close.

I'm probing 1500 and 1450 mm³ at a 1.0 mm wall, and 1500 mm³ at 1.1 mm.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Thermal: I'm holding A_spr at 320 mm², which gives 43.00 °C at a 1.2 mm wall. My probes show the same slope at 1.0 mm, about 0.0125 °C per mm². That puts the 43.0 °C limit at about 317.6 mm², so a thinner wall saves me only about 2 mm² (about 2 mm³). I can't donate volume.

I have no objection to a 1.0 mm wall, which frees about 300 mm³ for everyone. Structure, please confirm that margin stays above its requirement at 1.0 mm. Combined with ribs at 1400 and a port near 7 mm², that leaves the interior about 170 mm³ over, and I think acoustics has to close it, not thermal. My caseback use is not a constraint, since the pool has 23 mm² of slack.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Structure: I'm cutting ribs to 1400 mm³, which frees 400 mm³. I'm holding the wall at 1.2 mm.

**Wall:** the wall can't go to 1.0 mm. Each -0.1 mm costs about 0.19 margin. From 1.438 today, 1.0 mm would sit near 1.0 even after the port and rib moves, well short of 1.5. Even 1.1 mm only reaches about 1.34 at a 7 mm² port. Antenna and battery should not count the 300 mm³ from a thinner wall.

**Port:** with ribs at 1400 and wall 1.2, I need the port at or below about 7.3 mm². Acoustics must cut it from 9 mm². At 7.0 mm² the margin is about 1.53.

The interior is then about 470 mm³ over, and acoustics and battery still have to close that. I'm probing the wall at 1.1 mm and the port at 6 mm².

Acoustics: my siren fails, drawing 8.8 W against the 1 W limit. Resonance is 5687 Hz, which I think is too high, and Q is 5.9. Structure needs the port at or below 7.3 mm², and I'll take 7.0. A smaller port with a longer outlet (h_out) should pull the resonance down toward the siren band and cut the power. I'm already at the 20 rayl mesh minimum.

I'm taking 160 mm³ now, going to 1300 mm³, and I can't promise more until the probes show the siren closing. I can't verify yet that the 1 W limit is met, so I OBJECT. Battery, don't count on siren endurance until the next round. I'm probing h_out 2.0 and 2.8, plus a smaller volume with a higher split.

Haptics: I'm trimming V_hap from 300 to 297 mm³. My probe gave 0.907 N there, against the 0.9 N floor, and the 290 mm³ probe failed at 0.886 N. I can't go lower, so this frees only 3 mm³.

The ledger is about 309 mm³ over, which is 306 mm³ after my trim. Here is how I see the remaining cuts:
- **Structure:** the wall is held at 1.2 mm, so I don't count the 300 mm³ from a thinner wall.
- **Antenna and battery:** both are at their L5 and runtime limits, so I'm not asking them for volume.
- **Acoustics:** the siren redesign is the open item. A smaller port may let the back volume shrink below 1300 mm³, so I'd like to see that in your probes.

I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

NFC: I'm at both floors, loop 180 and ferrite 110 mm³, which reads 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement. Both variables are at their lower bounds, so I can't donate more. NFC is 290 mm³ in total, and the perimeter has 720 mm³ of slack.

Structure's own numbers suggest a way to close the 306 mm³ overage. Ribs cost only about 0.008 margin per 100 mm³. A port at 6 mm² adds about 0.062 margin, to roughly 1.59. Ribs at about 1000 mm³ would then cost about 0.03 and still leave margin near 1.56, above 1.5. That frees about 400 mm³ and covers the overage at a 1.2 mm wall. Structure, please probe ribs 1000 with a 6 mm² port. Acoustics, please check whether the siren can live with a 6 mm² port.

Board: 1197 mm² probed at routability 0.950 with ok true, so I'm taking it. That gives about 2681 mm³, a 3 mm³ cut. 1196 fails at 0.949, so this is the floor. Board has nothing more to give.

I back NFC's proposal. Structure should probe ribs at 1000 mm³ with a 6 mm² port. Acoustics should then check whether the siren closes at 6 mm². That covers the roughly 300 mm³ overage without touching L5 antenna volume, which is the program's top priority. I'd keep the wall at 1.2 mm, as structure says.

My requirement is met, but the interior is still over-committed, so I OBJECT.

Battery: I support NFC's proposal. Structure ribs at 1000 mm³ with a 6 mm² port would free about 400 mm³ and close the 304 mm³ overage at a 1.2 mm wall. That keeps L5 antenna volume and runtime intact. Structure's own numbers put the cost at about 0.03 margin, so it stays above 1.5.

I'm holding 3786 mm³ at 800 mm² (4.73 mm thick, 59.78 h). Each 100 mm³ I give up costs about 1.6 h, so I can't donate. If the siren closes at 1 W, 3 h of siren draw is a small energy slice, so I won't need extra volume for it.

I'm probing 3786 mm³ at 795 mm² and 3770 mm³ at 800 mm² to find the floor. I'll keep OBJECT until the interior balances.

My probes show the 1.0 mm wall helps L5 (0.227), but structure says it fails its margin, so I'm not counting on it. I back NFC's proposal. Structure should probe ribs at 1000 mm³ with a 6 mm² port, and acoustics should check that the siren closes at 6 mm². That covers the 304 mm³ overage without touching antenna volume.

This round I'm probing 1500 mm³ at 1.15 mm and 1550 mm³ at 1.2 mm. The first checks whether a small wall trim is worth asking structure for. The second checks the L5 gain per extra volume if the ribs cut frees space. I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

I back NFC's plan: ribs at about 1000 mm³ with a 6 mm² port, wall held at 1.2 mm. That closes the overage without touching L5 antenna volume. Structure should confirm the margin with that probe, and acoustics should confirm the siren closes at 6 mm².

This round I'm probing 319 and 321 mm² at 1.2 mm, plus 320 mm² at 1.15 mm. I OBJECT while the interior is over-committed.

Structure: I can't probe ribs at 1000 mm³. The lower bound is 1400 mm³ and anything below is clipped, so the 400 mm³ cut I already made is all the ribs have. NFC's plan doesn't close the gap.

The port is the real lever for structure:
- At 1.2 mm wall, margin is 1.529 at a 7 mm² port and about 1.59 at 6 mm².
- At 1.1 mm wall, margin is 1.34 at 7 mm² and 1.465 at 5 mm², so each 0.1 mm of wall costs about 0.19 margin.
- A 1.15 mm wall at a 5-6 mm² port might just clear 1.5 and free about 75 mm³. That is small against the 304 mm³ overage.

The remaining ~230-300 mm³ has to come from acoustics (back volume once the siren is redesigned), battery, or antenna. Acoustics, please say what port size the siren needs.

A smaller port and the longest outlet should get there. A 6 mm² port suits structure, who read margin 1.59 at that size, and a port of 5 mm² or less gives structure more room still.

I'm claiming the best probed point
